At Config 2026, we brought new tools and materials to the canvas to help you take your ideas further, faster. Where you go, though, is up to you.

## [Pick your own path](#pick-your-own-path)

That choose-your-own-adventure feeling inspired this year’s Config magazine, which lets you pick where to begin. Dive into the digital version to learn how teams are evolving old workflows to reach new heights.

## [What is taste, exactly?](#what-is-taste-exactly)

Figma’s Chief Design Officer Loredana Crisan argues that it’s not just knowing what’s good, but sustaining the energy to get there. Find out what playing music taught her about developing taste, and the three things she looks for when hiring new talent.

## [Rabbit hole](#rabbit-hole)

![1) Abstract graphic 2) a paper cup intersects with a photo of a mug 3) an orange T-shirt printed with a character doodling](data:image/png;base64,)![1) Abstract graphic 2) a paper cup intersects with a photo of a mug 3) an orange T-shirt printed with a character doodling](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/f3a9f3950e540d6e6ae7a0b5c07a89afeac4e06d-1296x726.png?rect=0,1,1296,725&w=804&h=450&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

1.  Our CEO and Co-founder, Dylan Field, [recaps everything we launched at Config](https://www.figma.com/blog/config-2026-recap/) and how we’re bringing new dimensions to the canvas.
2.  If you could build anything, what would it be? From systems that adapt to your mood, to tools that forecast the future, [our community imagines the future of software](https://www.figma.com/blog/future-states/).
3.  Season 5 of Figma swag just dropped. The eight illustrators behind the collection take us on [the journey from first sketch to the Figma Store](https://www.figma.com/blog/how-season-5-merch-came-to-life/).
